verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly ships an official CLI (ldcli) for managing flags, projects, environments and other resources from the command line. It also offers scoped API access tokens for building integrations and markets CI/CD pipeline integrations. Together these are the product's own building blocks for headless automation, but the evidence never documents a CI recipe or non-interactive auth flow for the CLI. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of running ldcli or the API in a CI pipeline (non-interactive auth, CI examples), a published OpenAPI spec (probes 404), and hands-on or independent corroboration of CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: set up and manage your feature flags, account members, projects, environments, teams, and other resources directly from the command line.
You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
Deploy code through your CI/CD tools. Your existing pipeline, now with the ability to control release behavior in production.
